Component: Frontend interaction events; authoritative backend lifecycle and ledger events
Design Requirement: Emit versioned events; backend is source of truth for transactional outcomes
Control / Risk: Do not emit credentials, full payment details or unnecessary personal data

Component: Authenticated event ingestion API / SDK gateway
Design Requirement: Validate schema version, required fields, event_id, timestamp, identity context
Control / Risk: Reject or quarantine invalid payloads; apply rate limits and access controls

Design Requirement: Retain original payload and ingestion metadata for replay/audit
Control / Risk: Restrict raw access; retention schedule approved by governance

Component: Schema, type, enum, duplicate, timestamp and referential checks
Design Requirement: Tag pass/fail with rule_id and reason; quarantine failed rows
Control / Risk: Never silently discard; monitor failure rates

Component: SQL/dbt-style transformations or equivalent lightweight scheduled jobs
Design Requirement: Standardise names/timezones, deduplicate, derive lifecycle facts and snapshots
Control / Risk: Version transformations; tests on key metrics

Component: Users, events, task activity, rewards, wallet, withdrawals, referrals marts
Design Requirement: Star-schema or clear relational facts/dimensions; stable keys and grain definitions
Control / Risk: No mixed-unit sums; maintain transaction lineage

Design Requirement: Role-based views; KPI catalogue definitions reused consistently
Control / Risk: Show data freshness and quality caveats

Component: Pipeline logs, data-quality metrics, alert channel
Design Requirement: Monitor freshness, volume anomalies, schema drift, failed jobs and late arrivals
Control / Risk: Owner, severity, runbook and recovery path per critical job

Component: Access review, retention, change control and audit logs
Design Requirement: Least privilege; documented metric/event versions; approval before breaking changes
Control / Risk: No production system or vendor is assumed to exist
